intent: My JITX build says status ok, but the inner ground pour captures as Empty(). Diagnose why no copper materialized.
Inspect the realized pour geometry after RuntimeDesign.capture and tell me why its type and area changed.
The via-stitch rule matched and the build passed, but it generated zero vias. Check the realized target and grid.
Verify that this KeepOut actually removed copper from the finished GND pour at every rank.
Pull this board-wide copper fill back from the profile and verify the final copper-to-edge gap.
Write a capture check that refuses Empty pours before calling to_shapely().
Why did floating=True make all my board pours and stitch vias disappear even though the design built?
Build a runtime probe for four Pour layers without reading Instantiable proxy attributes at module scope.
Draw a netless copper antenna that overlaps its feed and short pads without triggering copper overlap checks.
Create a custom polygonal copper shape with shapely and prove its realized bounds after capture.
Place these thermal vias in code, retain them structurally, and verify they survive the EDB export.
Author a code Route through control points and assert that every trace actually realized.
Add soldermask and paste openings to this custom thermal pad and validate the generated polygons.
Compute board-global pad positions for a composite landpattern so I can place escape vias correctly.
Set a rule that stitches every tagged ground pour with the preferred via on a 2 mm pitch.
Add thermal relief, direct-connect, and sliver-removal rules for the ground planes.
Choose the return layer and write trace-to-pour clearance rules for the high-voltage class.
Just connect GND and add a basic ground pour to the top-level circuit.
Wire this regulator, add its passives, and put the GND net on a simple return pour.
Define the six-layer stackup and the through, blind, and buried via classes.
Turn the fab report into FabricationConstraints, including minimum copper-to-edge spacing.
Create a fenced pour outline and select the substrate via definition for its fence rule.
Model this QFN component and its exposed thermal pad from the datasheet.
